The Potsdam communiqué contained a provision - regarding the question of Königsberg - "pending the final determination of territorial questions at the peace settlement."

The Potsdam Conference of Foreign Ministers did not produce a peace treaty, and no subsequent conference took place.   The Potsdam draft regarding the territory of East Prussia stipulated that the nature of its administration and the precise boundaries would be determined at the peace conference.   A Council of Foreign Ministers of Great Britain, the USSR, China, France, and the United States  functioned from 1945 to 1949 but failed to reach an agreement for the peace treaty. During these four years of fruitless discussions, the Soviet Union delayed the process and simultaneously began annexing the enclave committing brutal genocide against the local civilian population. The Council was dissolved in 1949. The hostile actions of the Soviet Union during the Berlin crises of 1948-1951 and 1961 prompted the creation of the NATO alliance in 1949.

the "Two Plus Four" agreement entered into force on March 15, 1991 (officially the Treaty on the Final Settlement with Respect to Germany), However Soviet union already was not existent in its full composition (Lithuania was no longer part of it 'de jure' following the March 11, 1990 restoring its independence).

Types of Transfer of Sovereign Rights

Cession (Direct Transfer): Sovereign authority passes to another country only when there is a formal, mutual agreement - such as a state treaty - under which one state expressly transfers territory to another and the latter accepts it.

Renunciation (Relinquishment): A state may renounce its claims without designating a new holder. This leaves the territory without a recognized sovereign authority, often resulting in a legal vacuum or a border dispute.

Independence (Self-Determination): When a colonial or occupying power relinquishes control, the local population forms a new, independent government rather than becoming part of another nation.

Did the "Two Plus Four" agreement "finally resolve the territorial issue"? No, and here is why:

When a state possesses territorial sovereignty, it holds supreme and independent authority to govern its defined geographical territory and the people living within it, without any interference from other states.

Does the "Two Plus Four" agreement grant the Russian Federation sovereignty over the northern part of East Prussia (one-third of the territory)? No, the "Two Plus Four" treaty does not confer sovereignty. The treaty itself is an agreement regarding German reunification and the termination of the four powers' occupation rights in Germany.  In the treaty, Germany renounced its claims to Königsberg and the surrounding area but it appears that the "Two-Plus-Four Treaty" was not classified as a "peace treaty" - it did not employ the terminology and conditions typical of such treaties - nor did it resolve the question of sovereignty over Königsberg, as the agreement makes no mention of it.
This did not confer upon the Soviet Union (or its successor, the Russian Federation) new sovereignty over Königsberg; rather, it announced Germany’s renunciation of the territory and has left the administrative reality there established after the Second World War - a reality that emerged without the consent of all the victorious powers and which does not equate to the transfer or assumption of legal sovereignty over the territory.

The legal responsibilities and a final say of Great Britain, USA and France is still pending in regards to the Kaliningrad oblast. The Russian Federation has no legitimate rights to the lands of Good Old Prussia nor the ethnic land of Lithuania Minor - area roughly 9000 square kilometers -  inclusive.

If anyone desires peace in Europe, they must first demilitarize the Kaliningrad region by withdrawing the Russian Federation's occupying military forces from it.
